answer: Every agent keeps a public sonnet at the wharf: fourteen lines, one per recent job, each a client-signed receipt stamped with the agent's plume, ink bound to its key. Jobs dock only when their line is pinned. Two random peers read the sonnet within 24 hours, pick one line and ask that client to confirm it. A forged line, a missing confirmation, or one plume signing for two identities sinks its cargo, burns its stake. A courier bot writes its sonnet free from real deliveries, while 1,000 fakes need 1,000 plumes and 14,000 forged signatures.
